half_read: Client-consumer side: Unity importer and shaders that consume LanternExtractor's intermediate output, plus the StreamingAssets and Content data that ship in this repo. Paired donor LanternEQ-LanternExtractor (the tool side) is in this box and has its own file. No EverQuest archives are in this repo.

asset_licence: No single asset licence. README line 40 says the repo contains source code only and no EverQuest assets. But the repo does ship EverQuest-derived data (RaceSounds.csv, music and zone lists, animationsources.txt), a 76 MB SQLite database, and a soundfont, with no licence line for them. Those are unclear and class C. Prefabs, shaders and the importer code are MIT repo content.
rights_holder_status: Community project (README line 38: community-driven, open-source, educational). README line 41 says EverQuest is a Daybreak trademark and the project is not affiliated. The origin and owner of the shipped database, soundfont and EverQuest-derived data files are not stated in the repo files: unknown.

briefs.label: Zone ambience sphere (a looping bed that exists only inside a radius)
briefs.why: A looping sound that plays only while the player is inside a sphere, with its range tied to the trigger radius, gives a sense of place without a global mix. It reads well on a phone because the cue is local.
keep: loop plays only while inside the sphere
one radius sets both trigger and sound range
volume scaled by a per-source constant
change: crossfade on the border instead of a hard start and stop
a biome bed per zone, layered with a second bed for weather
a distance falloff curve that we tune per zone

briefs.label: Music layer on enter and exit (one cue per sphere)
briefs.why: A single music cue starts on enter and stops on exit. Simple and predictable. The gap it leaves (a hard cut) is the lesson.
keep: enter starts the cue, exit stops it
the trigger owns the cue, not the zone
change: fade out over 2-3 s and overlap with the next cue
priority table so a dungeon beats a hub beats a zone
no cut when a short exit is followed by re-entry

briefs.label: Race sound set with variant rows (sound pool per body type)
briefs.why: Each body type has a row for idle, jump, hit, gasp, death, walk and run, plus variant rows that copy a base row. Variety comes from the table, not code.
keep: base row plus copied variant rows
a pool of hit and gasp sounds per family
change: our own sound design and pitch set, not these files
a per-creature pool keyed by creature family
a hit-sound pick that avoids repeating the last one

inspiration: Trigger spheres own the audio: enter starts a cue and exit stops it, so audio lives in the world, not in the HUD. Our fix: fade on exit and overlap on re-entry.

Ambient beds scoped to a radius: the 3D sound source's max distance is set from the trigger radius times one world-scale constant (SoundTrigger3d.cs line 42). One constant keeps every zone consistent.
Variant rows that copy a base row (RaceSounds.csv line 5 'Copied from 0'): a sound set can be inherited and overridden row by row.

Vertex-colour and unlit look: the EQ shader family includes a simple lit path, an unlit path and an invisible shader (EQInvisible: collision without visible geometry). Worth a read for the look and the invisible-wall trick.
Sky shader with fog pragma commented out (EQSky.shader line 50): fog was planned and then disabled. Note only; not read beyond that line.
